question.text: Let ABC be the triangle such that the equations of lines $A B$ and $A C$ be $3 y-x=2$ and $x+y=2$, respectively, and the points B and C lie on x -axis. If $P$ is the orthocentre of the triangle $A B C$, then the area of the triangle PBC is equal to

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Equation of Altitude } \mathrm{AP}: \mathrm{x}=1 \\ & \text { Equation of Altitude } \mathrm{BP}: \mathrm{y}-0=1(\mathrm{x}+2) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=1 \& \\ & \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}+2=0 \\ & \mathrm{P}(1,3) \\ & \text { Area of } \triangle \mathrm{PBC}=\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3=6\end{aligned}$
